from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup Title and Lecture
        title = Text("Introduction: From Sequential Reading to Global Context", font_size=28).to_edge(UP)
        lecture_lines = [
            "RNNs process text word by word sequentially.",
            "This approach limits understanding of global context.",
            "Transformers read entire sequences simultaneously instead."
        ]
        lecture = VGroup(*[Text(line, font_size=22) for line in lecture_lines])
        lecture.arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8).to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.5)
        self.add(title, lecture)

        # Create elements
        words = VGroup(*[Text("Word", font_size=24, color=YELLOW) for _ in range(3)])
        words.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5).shift(UP * 1.5)
        
        context_box = VGroup(
            Square(side_length=1.5, color=BLUE),
            Text("Context", font_size=20)
        ).shift(DOWN * 0.5)
        
        lines = VGroup(*[Line(start=words[i].get_bottom(), end=context_box.get_top(), color=BLUE) for i in range(3)])

        # Animations
        self.play(FadeIn(lecture[0]), Write(words))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(lecture[1]), Create(lines), FadeIn(context_box))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        glow = Dot(color=WHITE, radius=0.2).move_to(context_box.get_center())
        self.play(
            FadeIn(lecture[2]),
            context_box[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            FadeIn(glow)
        )
        
        self.play(
            lecture[0].animate.set_color(GRAY),
            lecture[1].animate.set_color(GRAY),
            lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Concept: Embeddings and Vector Space", [
            "Words are converted into multi-dimensional vectors.", 
            "Similar meanings cluster together in space.", 
            "Distances represent semantic relationships between concepts."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a vector as an arrow in #FF4500 from origin.

        self.play(Create(vec))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF4500")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Display multiple vectors clustered in a 2D space colored #32CD32.
        cluster = VGroup()
        for pos in ['B4', 'B5', 'C4', 'C5']:
            dot = Dot(self.grid[pos], color="#32CD32")
            arrow = Vector(self.grid[pos] - np.array([3.0, 0, 0]), color="#32CD32")
            cluster.add(dot, arrow)
        self.play(Create(cluster))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#32CD32")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight a specific vector point with a blue #1E90FF circle.
        highlight = Circle(radius=0.2, color="#1E90FF").move_to(self.grid['B4'])
        self.play(Create(highlight))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#1E90FF")

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Core Engine: Self-Attention Mechanism", [
            "Self-attention acts as a relevance map.", 
            "Each word attends to all others simultaneously.", 
            "Vectors determine contextual dependencies between words.", 
            "Query, Key, and Value models interactions.", 
            "Attention highlights specific, relevant information pathways."
        ])
        
        # Define elements
        q_box = Square(side_length=1.0, color=WHITE)
        q_text = Text("Q", color=WHITE).move_to(q_box.get_center())
        q_group = VGroup(q_box, q_text)
        
        k_box = Square(side_length=1.0, color=WHITE)
        k_text = Text("K", color=WHITE).move_to(k_box.get_center())
        k_group = VGroup(k_box, k_text)
        
        v_box = Square(side_length=1.0, color=WHITE)
        v_text = Text("V", color=WHITE).move_to(v_box.get_center())
        v_group = VGroup(v_box, v_text)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.play(FadeIn(q_group), FadeIn(k_group), FadeIn(v_group))
        self.place_at_grid(q_group, 'B2', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(k_group, 'B4', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(v_group, 'B6', scale_factor=0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF69B4")
        arrow1 = Arrow(q_group.get_center(), k_group.get_center(), color="#FF69B4")
        self.play(Create(arrow1))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFA500")
        heatmap = Rectangle(width=1.5, height=1.5, color="#FFA500", fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(heatmap, 'D3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(heatmap))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#00CED1")
        weight_text = MathTex(r"\sum w \cdot V", color="#00CED1")
        self.place_at_grid(weight_text, 'D5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(weight_text))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        final_box = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.2, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(final_box, 'E2', 'F5', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Create(final_box))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Scaling Up: From Transformer to LLM", [
            "Stacking layers builds deep pattern recognition.",
            "Training on massive datasets enhances reasoning.",
            "Models synthesize complex information across domains."
        ])
        
        # Create Transformer Block (Primitive representation)
        def create_block(color):
            rect = Rectangle(width=2, height=1, color=color, fill_opacity=0.3)
            label = Text("Block", font_size=20, color=color)
            return VGroup(rect, label)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        block = create_block(WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(block, 'C3')
        self.play(FadeIn(block))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        stack = VGroup()
        for i in range(5):
            b = create_block("#8A2BE2")
            stack.add(b)
        stack.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Transform(block, stack))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        data_flow = VGroup(*[Dot(color=WHITE, radius=0.05) for _ in range(10)])
        data_flow.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.2)
        
        self.place_in_area(data_flow, 'A2', 'F5')
        self.play(FadeIn(data_flow))
        self.play(data_flow.animate.shift(DOWN * 3), run_time=2)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(BLUE)
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion: The Generative Loop", [
            "LLMs use next token prediction generative loops.",
            "Probabilities determine the most likely continuation.",
            "The model builds stories through iterative prediction."
        ])
        
        # Assets
        llm_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/computer.svg")
        keyboard_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/keyboard.svg")
        
        # Animation Elements
        prompt = Text("Input Prompt", color="#FFFFFF")
        generated_word = Text("Next Word", color="#FFD700")
        loop_arrow = CurvedArrow(start_point=self.grid["C5"], end_point=self.grid["B3"], angle=-PI/2, color="#00FFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(llm_icon, "B3", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(prompt, "B4", scale_factor=0.4)
        self.play(FadeIn(llm_icon), Write(prompt))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(generated_word, "C5", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(generated_word))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(keyboard_icon, "D5", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(keyboard_icon), Create(loop_arrow))
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: Large Language Models (LLMs) and the Transformer Architecture
outline.target_audience: University students with a basic background in computer science

sections.title: Introduction: From Sequential Reading to Global Context
sections.content: Briefly explain the limitation of traditional RNNs (reading word-by-word) versus the Transformer's ability to process an entire sentence simultaneously, inspired by how humans scan a page.
sections.example: Comparing a person reading a book one word at a time versus a photographer taking a high-resolution snapshot of the entire page at once.

sections.title: Prerequisite Concept: Embeddings and Vector Space
sections.content: Introduce the idea of 'Semantic Space.' Explain that words are converted into multi-dimensional vectors where similar meanings (e.g., 'King' and 'Queen') are physically closer in space.
sections.example: Visualizing a 3D coordinate system where 'Dog' and 'Puppy' are clustered together as neighbors, while 'Toaster' is in a distant corner.

sections.title: The Core Engine: Self-Attention Mechanism
sections.content: Explain Self-Attention as a 'Relevance Map.' Every word looks at every other word in the sequence to determine the context. Mathematically, this is modeled as Dot-Product Attention: calculating Query, Key, and Value vectors.
sections.example: In the sentence 'The animal didn't cross the street because it was too tired,' the model draws a glowing line connecting 'it' to 'animal,' highlighting the dependency.

sections.title: Scaling Up: From Transformer to LLM
sections.content: Describe how stacking these Transformer blocks hundreds of layers deep, and training on massive datasets, allows the model to capture complex patterns, nuances, and reasoning.
sections.example: An 'AI Librarian' who has read every book in a massive library and can now synthesize information to write a poem or debug code.

sections.title: Conclusion: The Generative Loop
sections.content: Briefly demonstrate how LLMs use 'Next Token Prediction' to generate text, essentially playing a high-stakes game of 'guess the next word' based on the patterns learned.
sections.example: A robotic parrot that, instead of repeating phrases, predicts the most probable next word to complete a story based on everything it has learned previously.
